headline: All majors overbought above their 200-day lines while whales distribute into exchanges; funding hot and long-biased across the board.
paragraphs: Regime: All seven majors trade above their 200-day simple moving averages. None have completed a golden cross yet, so trend confirmation is incomplete, but the tape shows every asset in a higher-low pattern off the 12-month lows. Bitcoin is 36.1% below its 12-month high of $124,740; Ethereum sits 47.7% underwater; Solana is worst-hit at 60.8% from its peak at $247.60. The moves are recent and sharp: Bitcoin gained 26.48% over the last week and 24.99% in the month; Ethereum rose 33.02% in seven days and 38.55% in 30; XRP moved 51.56% in a week and 39.46% in a month. These are not slow recoveries. They are fast recoveries from deep drawdowns, which means the tape is measuring rebound strength, not new highs.

Momentum is screaming overbought. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 82.8, Ethereum at 80.0, Solana at 85.3, XRP at 85.7, BNB at 85.4, and Doge at 80.6. Only Cardano, which sits below its 200-day line, reads more moderately at 71.3. MACD is above signal for all seven. The speed of the rebound has compressed momentum into the overbought zone across the board. The risk here is not that momentum is broken, it is that momentum is matured. When every major asset carries an RSI above 80 on a multi-week uptrend, the probability of continued acceleration falls; the probability of consolidation, pullback, or exhaust rises. The contradiction worth naming: price momentum remains very strong, but the momentum indicator itself offers no room to run higher without a rest.

Leverage positioning shows funding rates locked in the 0.0097% to 0.01% per 8-hour window (10.6% to 11.0% annualized on OKX), which is expensive. Longs are paying to hold these bets. Bitcoin long-short ratio is 1.0, meaning the market is balanced at the perp level, but Ethereum longs outnumber shorts 1.17 to 1, and Solana and XRP are far more skewed: 1.9 to 1 and 2.04 to 1, respectively. Doge is heavily long-biased at 3.46 to 1. Open interest is substantial: Bitcoin at $2.34 billion, Ethereum at $1.50 billion. The boat is full, the funding is expensive, and the longer-duration assets (SOL, XRP, DOGE) show the most concentration of long bets. Liquidations over the last 4 to 24 hours show shorts being flushed more than longs in Bitcoin and Ethereum, but Solana and XRP are seeing more long liquidations than short, a sign that the long-heavy positions are being tested.

Whale flows tell a story at odds with the greed reading. Over the past 24 hours, $226.5 million moved off exchanges net, but the granular picture shows distribution: $145.99 million of Ethereum left Binance, and $233.48 million of Bitcoin left various venues (Binance and Kraken), partially offset by $152.95 million of Bitcoin moving back onto exchanges at OKX. The weekly picture is more telling: the week ending August 3 saw $1.085 billion move off exchanges, but the three weeks since (Aug 10, Aug 17, and Aug 24) show $379 million, $187 million, and $864 million moved BACK ONTO exchanges, respectively. That is $1.43 billion of selling pressure flowing into exchange wallets over the last three weeks. Whales are not holding; they are liquidating on rallies. Stablecoin reserves stand at $308.6 billion with negligible 30-day change (0.01%), so dry powder is flat. The buying power available ($236.6 million in one-day stablecoin moves) is thin relative to the asset volumes being moved off.

Spot ETF flows remain strong: Bitcoin saw $307.5 million net inflow on August 21, with five consecutive sessions of inflows totaling $1.918 billion. Ethereum took in $184 million on the same date, with five-session net of $692.6 million. Both metrics show same-direction consistency over five days. This is real money from traditional finance entering the market, and it has been persistent. The tension is direct: traditional finance is bidding assets higher (ETF flows, all-time cumulative Bitcoin inflows of $53.78 billion), but crypto natives on the whale tier are simultaneously stepping back and moving coins to cold storage or into exchange hoards as liquidity pools before exits.

Watch: whether the current week's whale flow reverses the three-week outflow-onto-exchanges trend. If off-exchange flows resume and stablecoin moves onto exchanges slow or reverse, the distribution thesis breaks and the tape tilts bullish. Conversely, if the pattern of coins flowing to exchanges persists while funding rates remain locked above 10% annualized, the overbought RSI clusters combined with expensive leverage positioning become a structural vulnerability. The golden cross never completed, and no major asset has printed a fresh 12-month high. Price above the 200-day is a win, but a win far from the summit is not the same as a new paradigm. Monitor the next five days of ETF flow direction (persistence or reversal) and the weekly whale flow bucket ending Aug 31 for the clearest signal of whether this rebound is accumulation or exit rally.
